checks.note: handleOAuthCallback's state check (P18 block) is confirmed weak — it only compares state to the victim's own predictable coachId with no nonce or single-use enforcement — but the exploit depends on JWTAuthorizationFilter/RequestMetadataProvider accepting cookie-only auth on this GET and on StripeOnboardingService.handleOAuthCallback/upsertCoachStripeAccount overwriting an existing stripeAccountId, none of which is in the shown file.

Router.beforeEach in index.js confirmably has no meta.role === 'COACH' branch and rolesMeta only reads plural meta.roles, so a role: 'COACH'-only route would be unguarded; but routes.js (to confirm /coach/revenue and the receipt route use role: 'COACH' rather than requiresCoach) and the backend @PreAuthorize scoping named in the verification caveat are not shown.

RateLimitingService.buckets (line 62) is indeed a per-JVM ConcurrentHashMap with no cross-instance coordination, so the consequence follows if replicas > 1 — but the finding's verification caveat (replica count / sticky routing) can't be settled here: the class Javadoc claims single-instance per docker-compose while the finding claims a multi-instance system brief, and neither artifact is shown.

AccountManagementFacade confirms sendPasswordResetMail/changeEmail/resendRegistrationLink are @RateLimited with no visible per-target-account throttle, but the finding hinges on RateLimitingAspect keying buckets by client IP with an 'unknown' fallback; that aspect's code (and the EmailRegistrationStrategy paths) is not provided, so the IP-only-keying claim cannot be verified or refuted from this file.

PasswordResetService.completePasswordReset indeed performs no revocation and injects no token/JWT collaborator, but the claimed consequence (old sessions staying valid) depends on User.completePasswordReset, JwtManagerImpl, and the token-validation path, none of which were provided — a credentials-updated-timestamp check there would refute the finding and cannot be excluded from this file alone.

updateUserEmail sets u.setEmail(newEmail) and u.setLogin(newEmail) immediately after a password + old-email check, with the AccountChangeEvent deliberately routed to capturedOldEmail only — so the change is applied without any proof of control of the new address, and no revocation or uniqueness pre-check appears in the method. The caveat's DB-constraint/HTTP-status and pending-state checks concern secondary details outside this file and don't affect the core consequence.

registerAccount calls findUserByEmailOrLogin using only userDTO.getEmail()/getLogin() before the else branch sets login = phone; with blank email and login the lookup runs as (null, null) and the phone column is never checked, so notifyUserExists is skipped and persistUser is attempted with login = phone. The verification caveat (users.login constraint, ApiAdvice rendering) only decides which of the finding's two stated outcomes — enumeration oracle or duplicate account — occurs, both of which it already claims disjunctively.

sendPasswordResetMail does return a shortCode on success and throw OperationNotAllowedException(PWD_RESET_REJECTED) on empty Optional, so a facade-level response divergence exists; but the claimed email+login+DOB filter and valid-outstanding-key rejection are inside PasswordResetService.prepareForPasswordReset/canInitiatePasswordReset, and the HTTP rendering of the exception is in an unshown handler — both required by the verification caveat and absent from this file.

DrillUploadService.initiateUpload validates and reserves only the client-declared req.fileSizeBytes and returns resp.signedUploadUrl() unmodified, confirming the trigger; but the finding's consequence depends on UploadCredentials.java's signature scope, videoService.initializeUpload, and the webhook/upload-confirm handler (whether it reconciles provider-reported size and invalidates TUS writes after READY) — none of which are in this file.

VideoTypeConstraints.validate rejects negative durations but applies the cap only under `durationSeconds > 0 && durationSeconds > maxDuration`, so durationSeconds=0 bypasses the configured max entirely. Per the verification caveat, no post-upload duration re-check exists in this file; one could exist in unshown webhook/processing code, but none is visible.

registerAccount's exists branch only calls strategy.notifyUserExists, while the new-user branch synchronously runs persistUser → userRegistrationService.createUser(toUser(userDTO), userDTO.getPassword()) plus publishEvent and notifyNewUser, all in the same @Transactional request; no dummy-hash, delay, or other timing-equalization code exists anywhere in the file despite the Javadoc's "timing-safe comparison" claim. The raw password passed to createUser and its immediately-used return confirm encoding/persistence happen in-request; only the exact bcrypt cost lives in UserRegistrationService (not shown), but the branch work asymmetry the finding describes is visible as stated.
